own_solution.law: The thin-lens equation gives di = f*do/(do-f). Initially di = 12*40/(40-12) = 120/7 cm. After the object's stand moves q farther along the axis, di = 12*(40+q)/(28+q).
assumptions: The standard thin-lens, paraxial model applies.
Moving the object's mounting stand carries the object along the optical axis.
The heights in the cancellation relations denote positive magnitudes.

notes: The claims agree with the locked pass-1 review. For either height sentence, substituting the similar-triangle relations gives di = do*(q*f/(do-f))/q, so the nonzero object height cancels at all three listed heights. The relations use image-height magnitudes; the real image is inverted. Moving the object's stand increases do to 45, 55 or 65 cm, yielding respectively 16.363636, 15.348837 and 14.716981 cm, consistent with every certified answer. Moving either unrelated stand has no stated optical coupling and preserves 120/7 cm. All listed object distances exceed the focal length, and the expressions have dimensions of length. The designated minimal pairs preserve the stated displacement and unit while changing which stand moves. The unrelated apparatus makes the additions slightly artificial but introduces no contradiction.
